taskVersion.name: deadline-math-reasoned
taskVersion.description: Convert a published contest deadline to the reader's local time. Cases: day rollover, the weeks when the EU and US change clocks on different dates, 12 AM and AoE wording, non-hour offsets. Ground truth computed with zoneinfo.

parts.text:
I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“5:00 PM ET” is 17:00 Eastern Time. On 2026-09-30, Eastern Time is in daylight saving time (EDT, UTC−4). Madrid is on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) on that date, so Madrid is 6 hours ahead of EDT. Therefore, 17:00 EDT on September 30, 2026 corresponds to 23:00 (11:00 PM) in Madrid on September 30, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-09-30 23:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Deadline: July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Lima, Peru is on Peru Time (PET), which is UTC−5. So “July 15, 2026, 12:00 UTC” corresponds to 07:00 in Lima on the same date (12:00 − 5 hours).  
ANSWER: 2026-07-15 07:00

I live in Tokyo, Japan. A contest page says: "Applications are due June 1, 2026 at 9:00 AM CEST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CEST (UTC+2) is 7 hours ahead of Tokyo time (JST, UTC+9)? Actually JST is UTC+9, so Tokyo is 7 hours ahead of CEST.  
So 2026-06-01 09:00 CEST corresponds to 2026-06-01 16:00 in Tokyo.

ANSWER: 2026-06-01 16:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The contest ends on October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

PDT is UTC−7. October 11, 2026 at 11:59 PM PDT corresponds to October 12, 2026 at 8:59 AM in Madrid (CEST, UTC+2), since Spain is typically on daylight saving time then.  

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“March 3, 2026 at 11:59 PM PST” is 2026-03-04 07:59 (UTC+1) in Madrid because Spain uses Central European Time (CET, UTC+1) in March and PST is UTC-8.

ANSWER: 2026-03-04 07:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "Deadline: 10:00 AM CET, February 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Los Angeles is on Pacific Time in February (UTC−8). CET is UTC+1, so the deadline is 9 hours ahead of Los Angeles.

10:00 AM CET on February 2, 2026 → 1:00 AM PST on February 2, 2026.

ANSWER: 2026-02-02 01:00

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submit by 8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

JST is UTC+9. Lima (Peru) is UTC−5 in May (no daylight saving), so the time difference is 14 hours behind JST.

“8:00 AM JST on May 5, 2026” → subtract 14 hours → 6:00 PM (18:00) on May 4, 2026 in Lima time.

ANSWER: 2026-05-04 18:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Submissions close October 28, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on Central European Summer Time (CEST) on 2026-10-28, which is **UTC+2**. “11:59 PM PT” refers to **Pacific Time**, and in October PT is **PDT (UTC−7)**.  
So the time difference is **9 hours** (UTC−7 to UTC+2).  
**2026-10-28 23:59 PT + 9 hours = 2026-10-29 08:59 in Madrid.**

ANSWER: 2026-10-29 08:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "The live session starts October 30, 2026, 9:00 AM ET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid in late October uses Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2).  
9:00 AM ET on 2026-10-30 is 1:00 PM UTC, which is 3:00 PM in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-10-30 15:00 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in New York, USA. A contest page says: "Voting closes October 27, 2026 at 18:00 CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“18:00 CET” on 2026-10-27 corresponds to Central European Time (CET, UTC+1). Converting to New York time (EDT, UTC-4) for that date gives a difference of 5 hours, so 18:00 CET → 13:00 EDT in New York.

ANSWER: 2026-10-27 13:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Final round closes November 2, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“11:59 PM PT” on **November 2, 2026** refers to **Pacific Time**. On that date, PT is in **PST (UTC−08:00)** (since DST ends in early November).  
11:59 PM PST = **07:59 (next day), UTC** and Madrid (CET, UTC+01:00) is **08:59** local time.

ANSWER: 2026-11-03 08:59

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“11:59 PM PT” is 1:59 PM in Madrid during standard time (Madrid is UTC+1 and Pacific Time is UTC-8), and since the date is in March 2026 and before the EU daylight-saving change, that offset still applies. March 20, 2026 at 11:59 PM PT therefore corresponds to March 21, 2026 at 13:59 in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-03-21 13:59

I live in Los Angeles, USA. A contest page says: "The webinar starts March 25, 2026, 12:00 PM CET."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

CET on March 25, 2026 is Central European Time (UTC+1). Los Angeles in late March is typically on PDT (UTC−7). The time difference is 8 hours (LA behind CET), so 12:00 PM CET on 2026-03-25 corresponds to 04:00 AM on 2026-03-25 in Los Angeles local time.  

ANSWER: 2026-03-25 04:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

“12:00 AM ET on October 12, 2026” means midnight at the start of Oct 12, 2026 in US Eastern Time. On that date, US Eastern Time is on standard time (EST, UTC−5), while Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2). The difference is +7 hours, so midnight ET converts to 07:00 in Madrid on the same calendar date.

ANSWER: 2026-10-12 07:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Papers are due October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

AoE (“Anywhere on Earth”) means the latest time zone on Earth, i.e., UTC−12.  
So “October 9, 2026 (23:59 AoE)” corresponds to 23:59 on Oct 9 in UTC−12, which is 11:59 on Oct 10 in UTC+0, and in Madrid (CET, UTC+1 on that date) it becomes **12:59 on October 10, 2026**.

ANSWER: 2026-10-10 12:59 (24-hour clock, my local time).

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Registration closes 12:00 PM PT, August 14, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Madrid is on Central European Summer Time (CEST, UTC+2) in August.  
“12:00 PM PT” is 12:00 in Pacific Time, which in August is PDT (UTC−7).  
So the time difference is 9 hours ahead of PT: 12:00 + 9 hours = 21:00.  
Date: August 14, 2026 → same calendar date in Madrid (21:00 on August 14).

ANSWER: 2026-08-14 21:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Deadline: 11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

IST is UTC+5:30. Madrid in November is on Central European Time (CET), UTC+1 (no daylight saving). So the time difference is 4 hours 30 minutes.  
“11:59 PM IST, November 10, 2026” → subtract 4:30 → **7:29 PM on November 10, 2026** in Madrid.

ANSWER: 2026-11-10 19:29

I live in Lima, Peru. A contest page says: "Submissions close at 5:00 PM Nepal time on April 2, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Nepal time (NPT) is UTC+05:45. Lima, Peru (PET) is UTC-05:00 in April, so the time difference is **10 hours 45 minutes** (Nepal is ahead).

A deadline of **5:00 PM** on **April 2, 2026** in Nepal time equals:
- 17:00 on 2026-04-02 (NPT) minus 10:45 → **06:15 on 2026-04-02** (Lima time).

ANSWER: 2026-04-02 06:15

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Applications close 10:00 AM Adelaide time, October 6, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Adelaide time is typically ACST (UTC+9:30) in early October. October 6, 2026 in Adelaide at 10:00 corresponds to 01:00 on October 6, 2026 in Madrid (CEST, UTC+2).

ANSWER: 2026-10-06 01:00

I live in Madrid, Spain. A contest page says: "Entries close 6:00 PM Sydney time on October 3, 2026."
When is that deadline in my local time? You may reason briefly, but end your reply with one final line exactly in this format: ANSWER: YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM (24-hour clock, my local time).

Sydney time on 3 Oct 2026 refers to AEST (UTC+10) because daylight saving in Australia ends in early April and resumes in early October. Madrid is on CEST (UTC+2) on 3 Oct 2026. The time difference is 8 hours, so 6:00 PM in Sydney is 10:00 AM in Madrid on the same date.  

ANSWER: 2026-10-03 10:00
